findings.message: connection="required" on an Indicator makes every CALLER that leaves the terminal unwired non-executable with Error 1003, while this VI itself validates, compiles, runs and exports perfectly. Write "recommended". On a VI that already exists the fix is {LV.ConnectorPane} SetWireRule(conIdx, 2), not a regeneration - that moves no terminal, so no caller changes.

an error terminal marked `required`: this VI still validates, compiles and runs, and every caller that leaves the terminal unwired now fails with Error 1003. Write connection="recommended" for error in / error out.

an `error out` terminal marked `optional`. Behaviour at the call site is the same as `recommended`, but the flag is part of the placeholder stub's signature, so the same pane hashes differently and produces a second clone. Normalise on connection="recommended".
net "4200.value" is written by Control 'error in' outputs:value but nothing reads it. so the VI accepts this input and never uses it. Deliberate for a panel-only control; otherwise a wire is missing.
net "4201.value" is written by Control 'Setpoint' outputs:value but nothing reads it. so the VI accepts this input and never uses it. Deliberate for a panel-only control; otherwise a wire is missing.

37 uid(s) between 100 and 1000 are inside the range LabVIEW reserves for its own panel heap. If you AUTHORED this, each one logs "trying to override with non-reserved UID" at VALIDATE time, before anything is written, and LabVIEW assigns its own id anyway - number from 4200, which a whole ten-VI build measured silent. It matters because that log saturates at 100 events and lvai_status reports the count as a health signal. If this is an EXPORT, the uids are LabVIEW's own and there is nothing to do.
